result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=without, B=with): Both answers choose a sidebar with one page per group, give each group its own URL, and describe the same sensible drill-down layout on phones. B ties its reasoning more closely to Driftline's content. It splits pages into narrow form pages and full-width list pages that can grow (vehicles, team, alert rules), and it plans for 200 vehicles, non-admin users and empty states. A treats the pages more uniformly, though its settings search is a useful addition. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): Both answers pick the sidebar with one page per group, give each group its own URL and use a drill-down list on phones, so they are close. A does better on the large groups: list-type pages like Vehicles, Team and Alert rules fill the width as tables, while form pages stay in a narrow column, and it flags stress cases such as a company with 200 vehicles. B adds useful extras (a settings search box, an exception for settings that apply instantly, a note on the build) but treats the large groups more lightly.
